LESSON: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: DIARY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary, part of Strand 12 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we plan our activities in advance? 2. What is the most memorable experience in your life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. view a sample diary sample journal/and identify the components,

2. write journal/diary entries with peers,

3. create an appointment diary collaboratively,

4. create a three-day journal with peers,

5. display their work in class and take a gallery walk,

6. give feedback to each group about their work after the gallery walk,

7. search for examples of diaries or journals on the internet, textbooks or the library,

8. create a diary or journal individually. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. view a sample diary sample journal/and identify the components,
2. write journal/diary entries with peers,
3. create an appointment diary collaboratively,
4. create a three-day journal with peers,
5. display their work in class and take a gallery walk,
6. give feedback to each group about their work after the gallery walk,
7. search for examples of diaries or journals on the internet, textbooks or the library,
8. create a diary or journal individually. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination is developed as the learner creates an appointment diary collaboratively.

Values:
Unity is fostered as learners create a three-day journal with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Life Skills Education - Effective communication is enhanced as the learner gives feedback to each group about their

work after the gallery walk.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The skill of writing diaries and journals is applied by the learner to other learning areas such as Kiswahili.
